source.title: Door input shows with no Room and sits badly at the window edge
source.body:
User report, from a screenshot: the input for the Door is badly placed, undesigned, and should appear only when a Room exists (a Workstream after #369).

Seen in the screenshot: with "no Room yet / + start a Room" in the centre, the Door input still shows at the bottom edge of the window. It touches the edge with no margin, wears a bare blue focus border, and carries an error line above it: "select a Room to talk to its Door". The input has focus before the user asked for it.

Expected:
- With no Room, no input and no error. The empty state offers the one entry point (#369).
- With a Room, the input sits inside the Room view with margin and a designed surface, Tokens only, and a clear send action.
- No input error for a state the UI can prevent.

Related: #355, #369, #389 (the Door receives the user's asks), #400.
Report only; no code change performed.

goals.statement: With no Room in the selection (an empty Project, no row selected, or a selected row with no Room among itself and its ancestors), the centre shows no Thread input, no feed, no send action and no input error; U143's `no Room yet` / `start a Room` is the only entry point in the centre.
goals.observer: U26 harness `?seed=empty-project` at 1280x800 and 700x800 in agent-browser: `document.querySelector('[data-thread-input]') === null`, no `.thread-failure` element, and the only centre button is `start a Room`; plus `u145_` Vitest for the empty-Project and root-Terminal-only cases.

goals.statement: With a Room selected (or a row inside one), the Thread's composer sits inside the centre, inset from its bottom, left and right edges by at least `--space-3`, on its own Token surface (`--sunken`, one 1 px `--hairline` border, `--radius-control`), with the one focus ring on the composer and no second outline on the bare input, and `window.__checks()` D1, D2, D6, D7 and D8 do not regress against main.
goals.observer: U26 harness `?seed=door-stopped` with its Room selected, at 1280x800 and 700x800: composer vs centre `getBoundingClientRect` insets, computed background/border/radius, focus look after Tab, and `window.__checks()` compared to main; captures in `artifacts/ux/U145/`.

goals.statement: A Room's composer has a clear send action: a native `send` button at its trailing end that sends exactly what Enter sends, and is disabled (`aria-disabled`, `--grey`, calls nothing) while there is no text, Quote or Attachment and while its `message.send` is pending.
goals.observer: `u145_` Vitest against the fake App seam: pointer, Enter and Space on `send` each make one `message.send` identical to Enter's; the empty state and a held `message.send` make none; harness capture shows the button.

goals.statement: No input error is shown for a state the UI can prevent: the string `select a Room to talk to its Door` is produced by no code path, and the failure line carries only what the UI cannot prevent, such as a rejected `message.send` (U80).
goals.observer: `git grep 'select a Room to talk to its Door' -- apps/` returns nothing on main; `u145_` Vitest asserts a rejected `message.send` shows its message and nothing else appears there.

goals.statement: The Thread's input never takes focus before the user asks: opening a Project, selecting a row by pointer, `start a Room` and starting its Door leave focus outside the Thread; only a pointer, Tab or `⌥0` focuses it.
goals.observer: `u145_` Vitest reading `document.activeElement` after each step; harness `document.activeElement` on load of `?seed=door-stopped` and `?seed=empty-project`.

deliveries.title: U145: the Thread's input shows only where it has a Door
deliveries.body:
## Outcome
The Thread mounts only when the selection resolves to a Room. Inside a Room its composer is inset, sits on a Token surface and has a `send` button. No code path shows an error for a state the UI could have prevented, and nothing moves focus into the input unasked. This implements U145 in `scenarios/ui-first-journey.md`, which is on main (found by #440).

On main 4597df41 the bug is still there. `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx` mounts `<Thread>` in every centre, including U143's `no Room yet`. `apps/desktop/src/thread/Thread.tsx` `submit()` sets `select a Room to talk to its Door` when `doorId()` is null. `thread/styles.css` gives `.thread-composer` no inset and no surface, and the input is transparent and borderless under the global `:focus-visible` ring.

## Scope
`apps/desktop/src/thread/**`, plus the one `<Thread>` mount in `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`. Move the `doorId` resolution (the selected Room, or the nearest Room above the selected row) to wherever it gates the mount. Remove the `select a Room…` branch. Style the composer with Tokens only. Add a native `send` button that calls the same submit as Enter. No contract, no RPC method, no App seam command, no new Token, no `GLOSSARY.md` change.

## Acceptance
- Every clause of U145 (No Room, A Room, Send, Focus, Errors) has a named `u145_…` test in `apps/desktop/src/thread/` against the fake App seam. The tests cover: an empty Project, a Project whose only row is a root Terminal, a selected Room, an Agent inside a Room, `send` by pointer, Enter and Space, its disabled states (nothing to send, a held `message.send`), focus after opening a Project and after `start a Room`, and a rejected `message.send`.
- `git grep 'select a Room to talk to its Door' -- apps/` returns nothing.
- U26 harness captures at 1280x800 and 700x800 go in `artifacts/ux/U145/`: `?seed=empty-project` with no `[data-thread-input]`, and `?seed=door-stopped` with its Room selected, showing composer insets of `--space-3` or more from `getBoundingClientRect`, its computed `--sunken` / `--hairline` / `--radius-control`, and `document.activeElement` on load.
- `window.__checks()` on those screens shows no regression against main for D1, D2, D6, D7 and D8. The PR body names the Checks it moves (rule 8).

Observer: the U145 observer in `scenarios/ui-first-journey.md`: `u145_` Vitest plus the agent-browser U26 harness readings above, compared with main.

## Preserve
- U105 dim, U106 fold and `⌃O`, U107 `⌥1`–`⌥9` / `⌥0` (with no Thread, `⌥0` ends a Takeover and focuses nothing), U109 Attachment and its non-image refusal line, U110 Quote, and U146's Message status. Keep the `u105_`, `u106_`, `u109_`, `u110_`, `u143_`, `u144_` and `u146_` tests green.
- U143's `no Room yet` / `start a Room` path and its Door state lines. The Pane keeps the space the Thread leaves.
- Direct Agent access (P1): `+ agent` and `+ terminal` stay unchanged.
- #379 still owns U105–U110 as a whole. This change edits only the Thread's mount, its composer and its error branch.
- #369 (Room becomes Workstream), #355 and #400 (window and button design) stay separate. Do not anticipate them.

## Queue
Scenarios: U145
Specification: [scenarios/ui-first-journey.md](https://github.com/saadshahd/roundup/blob/main/scenarios/ui-first-journey.md)
Key: U145
Priority: 20
Mode: implement
Provider: any

rules.content:
# UI: the first Room (U143)

Module: `apps/desktop` (the webview); U146 also edits the fake `claude` at `crates/rup/tests/e2e/fake_claude.py`. Ids: U143, U144, U145, U146. Found by walking the first journey in the U26 harness: an open Project with no row says only `select an agent or a terminal` and offers no first action in the centre; a Room whose Door is not running shows a bare `start Door`, so a Door that never launched, one that stopped, one that is starting and one that failed to start look the same.

**U143 the first Room says where it stands.** Narrows U38 and U9; changes no contract, App seam command or token. Given an open Project, then:

- **Empty.** Only when `rail.tree` has no row, the centre replaces U38's `select an agent or a terminal` with a light `no Room yet` and one button, `start a Room`. The button runs the same path as the Rail's `+ room` (U9): one `rail.createRoom {name: "room", parent: null}`, then select the returned Room once `rail.tree` has its row, then one `rail.startDoor {id}`. It is a native button, so Tab reaches it and Enter or Space activates it. While creation is pending the line reads `creating Room…`, the button is disabled, and a second activation of it or of `+ room` calls nothing (U9). A failed creation shows its message as an alert, selects nothing, starts no Door, and leaves the button ready to try again. A failed Door launch afterwards retries that same Room through U9's `retry Door`; it never creates another. With any row present and none selected, U38's text and no button show. The Rail's `no agents yet` / `⌘N starts one`, `+ agent` and `+ terminal` are unchanged, so direct Agent access stays.
- **Door states.** When the selected row is a Room whose Door has no running program, the centre shows one light state line above U9's `start Door` / `retry Door`, in a fixed block that does not resize the pane. The line is one of:
  - `starting Door…` while a `rail.startDoor` call is pending; the button is disabled, so a repeat activation calls nothing (U9);
  - `Door did not start` after a failed start (U9), beside the `✕ <message>` line and `retry Door`;
  - `Door not started` when the Room has no Attempt (A20) and no Terminal;
  - `Door stopped` when it has an Attempt and no running program, followed by `, exited <code>` or `, exited by signal` when the ending is known (U7's wording). `stopped` means launched before and not running now, however it ended, so a Room whose first launch failed reads `stopped` after a reload.
- **Running.** A Room with a running Door shows its Terminal and no state line. The words never mention a Thread or coordination: today the Thread is the Door's Terminal (`GLOSSARY.md`).
- **Direct access.** With a stopped Door selected, `+ agent` and `+ terminal` still spawn inside that Room (U9).

Tests are named `u143_…`: `apps/desktop/src/rail/doorState.test.ts` (the four states and their words) and `apps/desktop/src/terminal/u143_door_states.test.tsx` (the rendered App against the fake App seam, including keyboard focus, pending and repeat activation). Observer: the U26 harness at 1280 by 800 and 700 by 800, `?seed=agents-10` with its rows removed through `rail.remove` (an already open, empty Project), then `start a Room`, a failed start (`__fake.failNext`), the Rail menu's `stop`, and a `terminal.exited` with a code. `window.__checks()` must not regress against `main`: the full before/after readings and screenshots are in `artifacts/ux/U143/`. D1, D2, D7, D8 and D10 already fail on both observed screens; D6 additionally fails with a stopped Door. D3, D4, D5 and D9 stay passing. This scenario weakens no Check. Percy also captures the `empty-project` and `door-stopped` seeds, with the stopped Room selected before rendering. The native folder chooser is not covered by this browser observer. The fake answers at once, so `creating Room…` and `starting Door…` are observed in Vitest with a held promise, not in a screenshot.

Capability against UI. The Thread's input, Messages to a Door and Routes have contracts (`message.send`, `message.list`, `route.set`, `takeover.begin`, `decision.list`; `contracts/generated/methods.ts`). The Thread calls `message.send` and `message.list` (U105 to U110 in `ui-attention.md`, U145, U146), U107's jump calls `takeover.begin`, and U113's Cards call `decision.list`; no desktop UI calls `route.set`. U143 claims only the centre's first action and the Door's states. A summary of settled work (P1's observer) has no method; Todos have the Project-wide `todo.*` methods and a Shelf UI; their contract has no Room field. Room-scoped Todos need a contract decision before a Builder can implement them.

**U144 the harness serves the App on a real Daemon.** Found by the J2 audit: the Enter, Request and Review stages are observed only on the fake Daemon, because the webview reaches a Daemon only through Tauri commands (`apps/desktop/src/app/seam.ts`). Given a running `rupd` for a temporary Project and `just harness-real <project-path> <port>`, then `http://localhost:<port>/harness.html?daemon=1` mounts the same App with an AppSeam whose `rpc` and `subscribe` are served by the dev server over that `rupd`'s socket (`rpc::socket_path`) and whose `project`, `openProject` and `daemonProof` answer from the path given at start. Choosers return `null`, the Dock badge does nothing, and `daemon-exited` fires when the socket closes. Nothing else of the App differs, and `?seed=` behaves as today. It is a development tool: `vite build` leaves it out of `dist`, and it listens on loopback only.

Observer: `u144_` tests in `apps/desktop/src/testing/` start the real `rupd` with the fake `claude` of `crates/rup/tests/e2e/fake_claude.py`, mount the App through the served seam, create a Room and start its Door by pointer, and assert the Terminal and Rail row come from the Daemon, not from a seed. They then close the socket and assert the U25 failure state, and call a method the Daemon rejects and assert its message is shown. `agent-browser` captures at 1280 by 800 and 700 by 800 go to `artifacts/ux/U144/`. This is a webview proof against the real Daemon; the native chooser, WKWebView and a real `claude` remain the user's macOS and F7's observers. It adds no RPC method, App seam command or token.

**U145 the Thread's input shows only where it has a Door.** Found by the user's report #440: with `no Room yet` in the centre, the Thread's input still sat at the window's bottom edge with no margin, an outline on a borderless field, and the line `select a Room to talk to its Door` above it. Rule: a control shows only while the thing it acts on exists, and the UI never offers an action and then answers it with an error for a state the UI itself could have prevented. Narrows U105 to U110 and U143; changes no contract, App seam command or Token. Given an open Project, then:

- **No Room.** While the selection resolves to no Room (no row at all, no row selected, or a selected row with no Room among itself and its ancestors), the centre has no Thread: no `[data-thread-input]`, no feed, no failure line and no send action. U143's `no Room yet` and `start a Room` are the only action in the centre. `⌥0` (U107) still ends a Takeover and focuses nothing. No code path produces `select a Room to talk to its Door`.
- **A Room.** While the selected row is a Room or lies under one, whatever its Door's state (U143), the Thread shows inside the centre below the pane. Its composer is inset from the centre's bottom, left and right edges by `--space-3` or more, rests on its own surface (`--sunken`, one 1 px `--hairline` border, `--radius-control`), and uses only Tokens. When the input has keyboard focus the composer shows the one focus ring (`docs/design-system.md`, "Click targets") and the input draws no second outline.
- **Send.** A native `send` button sits at the composer's trailing end. Activating it, by pointer, Enter or Space, sends exactly what Enter in the input sends (U105, U109, U110). While the input is empty and no Quote or Attachment waits, and while a `message.send` it made is pending, it is disabled (`aria-disabled`, `--grey`) and calls nothing, so a repeat press sends no duplicate and shows no line. It meets D6 and D7.
- **Focus.** Opening a Project, selecting a row by pointer, creating a Room and starting its Door move no focus into the Thread. The input takes focus only from a pointer, Tab or `⌥0`.
- **Errors.** Only what the UI cannot prevent shows on U80's one line: a failed `message.send` with its message, and U109's refusal of a dropped file that is not an image. No other line shows there.

Tests are named `u145_…` in `apps/desktop/src/thread/` against the fake App seam: an empty Project, a Project whose only row is a root Terminal, a selected Room, an Agent inside a Room, the send button by pointer and keyboard, its disabled states (nothing to send, and a held `message.send`), the focus after `start a Room`, and a rejected `message.send`. Observer: the U26 harness at 1280 by 800 and 700 by 800 with `?seed=empty-project` (no Thread in the DOM) and `?seed=door-stopped` with its Room selected (the composer's insets read from `getBoundingClientRect`, its computed surface, and `document.activeElement` before any input). `window.__checks()` must not regress against `main` for D1, D2, D6, D7 and D8; captures go to `artifacts/ux/U145/`. Room becoming Workstream (#369) renames this scenario's words with every other one and does not change it.

**U146 a Door answers a Thread message in the real-Daemon harness.** Found by the J3 audit: on `just harness-real`, a Message sent to a started Room's Door reaches the Daemon and shows in the Thread, but the fake `claude` of `crates/rup/tests/e2e/fake_claude.py` is scripted only by its environment at start, so it never reads what is typed and takes no action, the Room stays `starting`, and no Todo or outcome can be observed. Changes no contract, App seam command or token. Given `FAKE_CLAUDE_ON_PROMPT`, a JSON `{"name", "arguments"}` tool call, then:

- **The fake.** After its session starts, the fake plays `UserPromptSubmit`, then the tool call with `"$prompt"` in an argument replaced by the typed text, then `Stop`, once per prompt line typed into its Terminal. Without the variable it behaves as today.
- **The Message.** The Message to the Door goes `pending` to `delivered` (B1, `docs/messages.md`) once the Door is idle, and the Thread shows its status beside it.
- **The Todo.** A `todo_create {title: "$prompt"}` call puts that Todo in the Shelf's `todos` and the Room's status returns to `idle` with no reload.

Observer: `u146_` tests in `apps/desktop/src/testing/` start the real `rupd` as U144 does with `FAKE_CLAUDE_ON_PROMPT` set to a `todo_create` call with `"$prompt"` as its `title`, mount the App through the served seam, create a Room, start its Door, send `ship j3` by pointer, and assert the Message is `delivered`, the Todo `ship j3` shows in `todos`, and the Room is not `starting`; a reopen of the Project finds both again (A8, S5). `agent-browser` captures at 1280 by 800 and 700 by 800 go to `artifacts/ux/U146/`. A real `claude` stays F7's observer.
rules.cases:
Recovery of PR #444 (merged without independent approval): it put U145 and the `Ids:` change on main. This proposal keeps U145's intent and corrects it. (1) Send: the button is also disabled while its `message.send` is pending, as the plan's own probe 10 required, so a repeat press makes no duplicate and no error. (2) Errors: U109's non-image refusal is named as allowed, because the UI cannot know a file's kind before the drop. Before, the clause banned every line but a failed send, which contradicted U109. (3) The stale 'Capability against UI' paragraph is corrected: it said no desktop UI calls `message.send`, but on main 4597df41 `thread/Thread.tsx` calls `message.send`, `thread/feed.ts` calls `message.list`, `rail/Jump.tsx` calls `takeover.begin` and `decisions/decisions.ts` calls `decision.list`. `route.set` has no caller. (4) The test list adds the held-send disabled state. Nothing else changes.
Rule: a control shows only while the thing it acts on exists, and the UI never offers an action and then answers it with an error for a state the UI itself could have prevented.
Cases:
- #440: Thread input with no Room. Wrong: input shown, then `select a Room to talk to its Door` on submit. Right: no Thread; `start a Room` is the entry point.
- A root Terminal is selected with no Room above it (`doorId()` is null). Wrong: the same error. Right: no Thread.
- U143 `start a Room` / `start Door` while pending. Right (already on main): disabled, calls nothing.
- A rejected `message.send`. The UI cannot prevent it, so its line is allowed.
- U109: a non-image file is dropped. The UI cannot prevent it, so the refusal line is allowed.
Probes:
1. `send` with nothing to send: disabled, no call, no line.
2. `send` pressed twice while the first send is pending: one call, no line.
3. The selected Room is removed while text is typed: the Thread unmounts, no error.
4. A stopped Door's Room is selected: the Thread shows, and refusing the send is the Daemon's call.
5. `⌥0` with no Room: ends any Takeover, focuses nothing.
6. Quote from a Terminal selection with no Room: there is no input, so no Quote is made.
7. The Daemon exits (U25): the exit line shows, because the UI cannot prevent it.
Counterexample hunted: `⌥1`–`⌥9` to an Agent whose `takeover.begin` answers CONFLICT (U107). The UI cannot know the Agent ended, so the error is allowed under 'could have prevented'. No narrowing is needed.
